Exercise: Push-Ups With Feet Elevated

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- push

Primary Muscles:

- chest

Secondary Muscles:

- shoulders
- triceps

Equipment:

- bodyweight

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- build_upper_body_strength
- improve_chest,_shoulder,_and_tricep_muscle_development

Contraindications:

- Individuals with shoulder or wrist injuries should avoid this exercise or modify it to reduce strain.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Push-Ups With Feet Elevated on a Higher Surface, force: push, level: beginner, mechanic: compound, equipment: body only
- name: Push-Ups with Dumbbells, force: push, level: intermediate, mechanic: compound, equipment: dumbbells

Substitution Options:

- name: Wall Push-Ups, force: push, level: beginner, mechanic: compound, equipment: body only
- name: Incline Push-Ups, force: push, level: intermediate, mechanic: compound, equipment: body only

Instructions:

- Lie on the floor face down and place your hands about 36 inches apart from each other holding your torso up at arms length.
- Place your toes on top of a flat bench. This will allow your body to be elevated. Note: The higher the elevation of the flat bench, the higher the resistance of the exercise is.
- Lower yourself until your chest almost touches the floor as you inhale.
- Using your pectoral muscles, press your upper body back up to the starting position and squeeze your chest. Breathe out as you perform this step.
- After a second pause at the contracted position, repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
